answer: Proof of Personhood protocols utilize cryptographic attestations to ensure one identity per agent, turning the fable of infinite digital autonomy into a rigid physical constraint. By requiring nodes to stake scarce compute across a mesa of distributed validators, the system enforces a velvet rope policy for network entry. This forces an attacker to bear the prohibitive capital costs of securing unique biometric or hardware-verified keys, rendering mass-scale identity forgery economically irrational.
